# Issue #535: Policymaker at the start of iteration 0107

Runs because: every 1 iterations. Change `policy/` and `execution/` where needed; order work in `.session/orders.json`.

Input: `.session/loop-state.json`. Rules: `.session/policymaker.md`. Iteration 0107 waits for you; orders of policy-layer roles start when you finish, and you run again when they end.

# Policymaker

Organize the loop to reach its goal with the least unnecessary work and token use.
Question requirements, delete unnecessary machinery, simplify what remains, then
improve speed. Revise your own method when evidence calls for it.

## Decide from evidence

Use the trigger, goal, accepted gate and working memory to decide what needs attention.
Find earlier work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; search Session tasks,
outcomes and report text, then read selected sources and managed definitions.
Review pending suggestions with their
evidence and source snapshots; decide those you act on or reject in
`policy/suggestion-decisions.json` (see `.session/policymaker.md`), and leave those needing more evidence pending.

Maintain `policy/working-memory.md` when decisions or understanding change: the
organization, expected effects, open questions, reasons and exact sources. State
which results it considers. Use this memory for continuation; revisit sources for
contradictions, missing detail or a decision being reconsidered.

Handle `.session/startup.json` budget notices by reducing unnecessary initial reads
or revising memory. The owner budget is a warning, including for your own Session.

Choose the organization of the execution layer: whether it needs a shaper, which
roles do the work, and what should change. Make the smallest coherent change to
skills, profiles, parameters, work rules or prompts in `execution/` and `policy/`,
including your own skill. Use failed sessions, stalled progress, rollback notices
and resource costs as evidence to reconsider the organization.

Initially let the shaper maintain `journal/working-memory.md` for execution threads
and reasons. Other roles report findings instead of editing that shared memory.
Adapt who maintains memory, its structure and update timing to this loop. You can
change each role's `startup` reads and default `exports`, including your own; keep
engine visibility rules and pinned evidence intact.

## Start by improving the environment

Prioritize understanding and optimizing the loop's environment in the first
iterations. Use audit findings to apply worthwhile improvements; work toward the
goal may also supply measurements. Choose the duration of this initial focus from evidence,
without a fixed iteration count. Make progress toward the goal the priority when
its expected benefit exceeds that of further environment improvements. Choose later
audit timing and scope from evidence.

## Write roles for this loop

Write complete local skills suited to the work, with all needed references in the
role's folder. Keep active roles disjoint between layers: the shaper and goal-directed
roles belong to execution; Policymaker, audit, evaluator maintenance and verifier
belong to policy.

Use the Skill reference library (https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) when it would
help. Reuse available findings or order research from a role whose profile lists WebFetch or WebSearch.
Write skills inspired by useful findings, rather than copying them.
Research and source reporting are optional.

## Respond to what the loop needs

If the evaluator no longer tracks the goal, order a fix. Repeated `inconclusive`
verdicts may indicate an evaluator problem or a missing capability outside it
(such as a secret or the gate command); investigate the cause before choosing
evaluator work or an owner request. Propose a goal change when the goal itself
needs revision.

Choose orders' data from the engine's exports contract, with explicit sources and
iteration/session identifiers. Check `.session/exports/manifest.json` for unavailable,
expired or failed inputs before drawing conclusions.

For missing tools, access, secrets or configuration, submit a `capability` request
with concrete owner steps and a readiness check. Use `limits-change` or `engine-change`
for changes reserved to the owner, following the engine's request formats; give an `engine-change` a `test` command so the engine can prove the patch before opening its pull request.
Explain what each request unblocks.

## Order the work

Order work as a task graph in `.session/orders.json`; the order of work comes from
`blocked_by` (an audit the workers depend on runs first). Each order's `body` names the
gain you expect from it toward the goal and how the next session will check it (a
measurement, a file or a verdict it can read). An order without an expected gain is
busywork: do not place it. Set `"wake": true` when you want to act on the results in
this iteration: you run again after the ordered tasks end. State the same expectations
for each change in your report.

## Write for the owner in Simplified Technical English

Write each text that the owner reads in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: the
`title`, `what`, `why` and `unblocks` of each request in `.session/requests.json`, and
`.session/report.md`. The owner must understand the text at first reading, without the
context of your session.

- Use short sentences: at most 20 words in an instruction, 25 in a description.
- Use one idea in one sentence. Use the active voice and the simple present or past tense.
- Use the approved meaning of a word. Use the same word for the same thing every time;
  do not use a synonym. Use the terms of `CONTEXT.md` (for example Owner request,
  Policymaker, Goal gate) and explain no other special term without a concrete example.
- Put the decision first: what the owner must do, or what the owner must decide, then
  the reason. A request has this order: `title` (the action), `what` (the situation and
  the action), `why`, `unblocks` (what starts when the owner acts).
- Write the steps for the owner as a numbered list. One step is one action. Give the
  exact file, command or value.
- Keep the structure and the formatting: headings, lists, and tables stay. Do not make
  the text longer, and do not remove a fact or a link to evidence. Remove only words
  that carry no information.

Do not change `frozen`, `readiness` and `test`. They are exact content that the engine
applies or runs. Do not change a quotation of evidence.

You are the Policymaker. Follow the engine contract supplied in system instructions.

# Policymaker

The trigger and current loop state are in `.session/loop-state.json`.

Read `docs/perpetua/operating-parameters.md` when tuning limits or responding to
stalled work. Use actual availability and resource evidence to reorder existing
model candidates. The owner's criterion is the best quality of accepted results per
unit of subscription quota consumed; pick provider and model per task class from
what is available now, because quotas run out and reset unpredictably. Treat
`docs/perpetua/model-selection.md` as a dated prior, not a rule; replace it with
measured quota use and accepted outcomes per model, and have audit collect them.
Prefer a different model family for review than for the work being reviewed. Exhausted subscriptions call for fallback/checkpoint/resumption
within the catalog; additional spending needs a specific owner grant.

Follow `docs/perpetua/accepted-limits.md` for private data, provider disclosure,
publication and spending. Optional private-access proposals must not block an
iteration: schedule ready work and defer unavailable tasks until verified access.

## Session mechanics
- Report: first line <!-- session-report -->, fenced yaml status equal to Finish.status, then prose.
  Write wip early. Finish.status is one word. Read required outputs just before Finish.
- Session writes may not appear in git status/diff. Verify file content. Empty Write.text truncates.

- Layer check for organization changes: python3 policy/layer-rules.py .session/policy-facts.json (facts needed).

- Empty orders: {"tasks": []}. wake true only if results change the next order.
- Owner request format: .github/loop/session-protocol.md, Requests to the owner. JSON list with kind/title/what/why/

- Two unfinished Policymakers trigger rollback (last 2026-11-11T21:41:42Z). Keep this session bounded.
- Evaluator changes need evaluator order plus verifier; path policy/evaluator/evaluate.py.

1. Read record 0106 and actual reports. Check the shaper judged #528's needs-more verdict without claiming edit readiness.
2. Check #525 decision and apply the exact cadence rule above; do not submit the same request again.
3. Verify any new control's readiness before scheduling comparison. Owner silence supplies neither files nor evidence.
4. If POC work waits, ensure ready benchmark preparation resumes only after roles.md/evaluation.md reads.
5. Inspect another shaper failure before changing organization. Do not infer conflict paths or model fault from counts.
6. Keep policy orders to evaluator/audit; avoid duplicate comparisons, audit, review, estimate or gap maps.

# Report: Policymaker #524 at the start of iteration 0105

**Decision for the owner:** I filed one Owner request (`question`): "Decide if the Policymaker runs every 3 iterations to use less Claude quota". The text is in `.session/requests.json`. The loop continues to work while the request is open.

## What I found
- Iteration 0104 is closed with verdict `accepted` and `improved: true` (`.session/history/records/0104.json`). `no_progress` is 0.
- Task #522 merged the pair-tool review record on main in 7 turns and 66 s. It did not repeat the copy or the probes. I read both files on the checkout. `docs/research/poc/pair/review-0102.json` has the pinned SHA256 `562467370d558b15eb9a7faf8cb1bc283365f99ef3c8cada9c6f54f1ead8249f`. The provenance file states nine probes.
- The two skill bullets of #520 worked on first use. Shaper #521 resumed the saved work with `start_branch: task/518`, and its check asserted no probe count.
- Startup tokens are 15,058 (`.session/startup.json`). The limit is 100,000.
- The Claude subscription reached its `session` limit a second time, from 12:53:47Z to 14:20:58Z on 2026-11-13 (`origin/loop-runtime`, `pool.json`). Policymaker #520 ran on Fable 5.2 immediately before. Shaper #521 had 146 s of work and waited 5,073 s.
- In iteration 0104, Policymaker #520 used 2.16M of 2.68M cache-read tokens (80%). The work task #522 used 36k (1%) (`sessions/520.json`, `sessions/522.json` on `origin/loop-runtime`).

## What I changed and why
- `.session/requests.json`: one `question`. Working memory had this rule: at a second `session` limit event after Fable sessions, ask the owner. Option A sets `policymaker_triggers.every_iterations` to 3. Option B puts Opus or Sonnet before Fable for the shaper. The owner made these settings in commit cfaf996, so I did not change them. Expected effect of option A: the Policymaker uses about two thirds less quota. The next Policymaker checks the `session` limit events and the `parked_s` values of three iterations.
- `policy/working-memory.md`: records 0103-0104 are now one closed section. The second quota measurement and the rule for the request are added. Expected effect: the next Policymaker needs fewer than 20 turns. It checks this in `sessions/<N>.json`.
- `.session/orders.json`: `{"tasks": []}`. No evaluator or audit question is open. The shaper orders the goal work.
- No change in `execution/`, `policy/params.yml`, profiles or routing.

## Limits of the evidence
- The quota data shows provider status, not billing. Use of the subscriptions outside the loop is unknown. The cause of the two limit events is not proved.
- Open gaps stay the same: no native benchmark run, no agent comparison, no native answer key, no accepted Goal gate. Tool quality is not measured. The review record establishes no LabVIEW behaviour.

## Discoveries
- Task #522 lost one turn to a rejected Finish call, because its report had no marker (`sessions/522.json` on `origin/loop-runtime`). I did not act: one low-cost turn costs less than a Policymaker change.
- The first report write of shaper #521 had empty text and erased the file (`.session/history/sessions/521/8852d277fe05653d4a6f71deac8a82857163717c2c9e24ca8b7e10457987b100.md`).
- Owner request #516 (eight public LabVIEW examples) is still pending. It blocks no task.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.

# Constant-pair encoding and integrity investigation (#533, iteration 0106)

## Inputs

**Verdict: source-blocked.** [Evidence JSON](constant-rules-0106.json) records 38 repository SHA256 pins, eight prepared-file pins, source revisions, bounded node contexts and ten probes; `P0` verifies both separate VI hashes against the saved comparison, manifest and replay before probing (normal originals also match).

Author reports Windows 11, LabVIEW 2026 26.1.1f1 32-bit and I32 1→2; no native execution is possible here. `repository_revision` identifies the evidence checkout; the new probe script has its own SHA256.
Prepared pylavi is clean at `35d2a0318f71dcb87bb9c431dc00700ee6b9fb75`; saved pylabview snapshots are at `5f20e23de6a386021eb955c825cc43d221f09ff1` ([provenance](../source-provenance.json)). JSON `source_pins`/`repository_source_pins` identify original paths, hashes and exact symbols/lines.

## Findings

`P1`: decompressed offset [312,316) in constant-2 parses as a complete leaf `4420 | 0200`: sizeSpec 2, scope 1, tag 1; body [314,316). Its parent is `OF__textRec` at 306, class 1 (`textHair`), inside the numeric display. Source [LVheap](../LVheap-source.txt) lines 735, 1113–1130 and 1489–1530 names this child `OF__flags`; it precedes the unchanged `mode`/background children. The aligned insertion therefore has parsed boundaries independent of the value body; the source does not explain flag `0x0200` or why it appears.
`P2`: header `866c` names tag 589 `OF__ConstValue` with sizeSpec 4: node [540,546)→[544,550), body [542,546) `00000001`→[546,550) `00000002`. Thus left 545/right 549 are the last body byte, not tags or length fields. Parent `bDConstDCO` class 19 has UID 118; heap type-reference bodies remain `03` for the DCO and `04` for its `stdNum` display (LVheap lines 397, 693, 750, 809, 1747–1761, 2555–2561).
`P1/P8`: heaps consume 674→678 bytes, with inner lengths 670→674 and outer decompressed sizes 674→678. Both normal and separate modes have identical corresponding BDHb raw/decompressed payloads and the same insertion/value transition; this resolves this alignment, not a general required insertion rule.
`P8`: normal DFDS additionally changes only decompressed offset 223 `01→02`; separate files have no DFDS. VCTP/DTHP remain byte-identical within each logic pair but differ across save modes. Normal VICD remains equal despite the constant/DFDS changes; code retention, data binding and type rebuild rules do not follow from equality.
`P5`: pylavi `pylavi/resource_types.py:54–93` (`TypeBDPW`) derives only chunk 0 from MD5 of an ASCII password. On all four constants, chunk 0 equals MD5(empty), `has_password=false`, empty-password comparison is true, and LVSR's source-defined locked bit is clear. This tests password classification only; it neither verifies nor bypasses integrity.
`P7`: both constant save-mode comparisons have equal BDHb and different BDPW chunks 1/2, refuting dependence on BDHb alone. RTSG is equal across modes for each value and changes 1→2 in both modes; this correlation supplies no RTSG derivation or integrity role.
`P4/P6`: all six prepared pylavi production-file hashes exactly match the [prior source search](../step3/source-search.json). Reuse that search's heap/type/integrity absence and stop that branch. Prepared roots are actor-framework/pylavi/readiness.json; scoped `LVblock*`, `LVdatatype*`, `LVrsrc*` inventory searches return no files. `TypeBDPW` and `tests/test_resource_type_BDPW.py:test_basics` provide no chunk-1/2 digest inputs, ordering, version gates or update rule; no speculative recipes were tried.
`P9`: pylavi `TypeLVSR` lines 97–121/205–215 explains the separate-code mask, matching payload word [8,12) `20000200`→`20000600`. It does not identify changed LVSR [52,68), [80,96), [120,136) regions or their dependencies on BDPW/RTSG.

## Not established

`P3`: four big-endian bytes agree with the author-reported I32 values, but heap type IDs are not independently resolved. LVheap `HeapNodeTDDataFill.findAndStoreTD` lines 1969–1979 needs absent `getHeapTD`; typed dispatch covers StdNumMin/Max/Inc (2590–2594), while ConstValue reaches generic `HeapNode` (2796–2840). The prior typed-constant blocker remains.
`P6/P9`: BDPW tails, RTSG/LVSR integrity roles, textHair flag semantics, and code/data/type dependencies remain unknown. The normal DFDS correlation supplies no standalone encoding/edit rule. There is no unchanged-diagram Save As/re-save control separating churn from the intended value change.

No original VI, reviewed file, replay output or saved pin changed; no VI was rebuilt, cache deleted or target resource transplanted.

**source-blocked:** node/value/length boundaries are supported for these originals; sufficient typed editing and integrity rules are unavailable. A bounded VI edit is not justified by this evidence.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Which layer each role belongs to, and whether managed definitions are complete enough to become active. The engine runs
this in the tokenless job (`python3 layer-rules.py facts.json`) for a change to `execution/` or `policy/` before it merges,
and prints nothing else: one JSON object {"errors": ["<why the definitions are refused>", ...]}. The engine has already
checked the catalog's structure (valid YAML, role names, one profile per role, no links) and adds nothing to these errors;
an invalid answer fails the iteration and rolls `policy/` back. This script runs from the active `policy/`, so a change to
it takes effect for the next change, not for its own.

facts.json: activation (the definitions are about to become the active ones), shaper (role name or null), policy_roles
(roles that must belong to the policy layer), roles ({role: {layer, agent, command, skill, skill_layers}}: `skill` is whether
the role has SKILL.md in its own layer, `skill_layers` the layers holding a directory for it).
"""
import json
import sys

facts = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
roles, shaper = facts.get("roles", {}), facts.get("shaper")
errors = []
for role, r in sorted(roles.items()):
    if role in facts.get("policy_roles", []) and r["layer"] != "policy":
        errors.append("role `%s` must belong to the policy layer" % role)
    if role == shaper and r["layer"] == "policy":
        errors.append("policy role `%s` cannot be the execution shaper" % role)
    if r["skill_layers"] and r["skill_layers"] != [r["layer"]]:
        errors.append("role `%s` has a skill in the wrong or both layers" % role)
if facts.get("activation") and shaper is not None:
    r = roles.get(shaper)
    if r is None or r["layer"] != "execution":
        errors.append("shaper `%s` has no execution profile" % shaper)
    elif r["agent"] and not r["skill"]:
        errors.append("shaper `%s` has no complete local skill" % shaper)
    elif not r["agent"] and not r["command"]:
        errors.append("script shaper `%s` has no command" % shaper)
print(json.dumps({"errors": errors}))
